| One job without a mouse      | **Done, and it produced [319].** The job itself finished end to end: ⌘K → `Marlow` → Enter opened the product; Tab to the pane tabs, Right Right to Variants (focus moved, the panel did not, which is the correct manual-activation pattern), Enter; Tab to **XS · Oat**, which took a clear ring around the whole row; Enter expanded it; Tab into Price; `102.00`; Shift+Tab to Save; Enter. Every unsaved signal fired together — row badge, "1 version has unsaved changes", a dot on the Variants tab AND on the pane tab, the status-strip line, Save going live — and every one cleared on save; the database reads `10200`. What was broken is the distance: **62 Tab presses** to reach the pane at all, ~15 through the rail and three per open pane through the tab strip, thirty of them close buttons, with no skip control and F6 doing nothing. Fixed with a skip control that appears at Tab 2. It jumps the rail and **not** the tab strip, because landing past the strip means knowing which pane is active and that is dockview's to say — recorded that way in the code and the issue rather than faked. _Also observed, not proven:_ Ctrl+S does not save, it typed an `s` into the price field which the field sanitized away on blur; may be an artifact of how the automation delivers modifiers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

At her real volume the lists are not the problem. What the check DID find is that the Customers list opened on the wrong people: sorted by **Recent order**, every one of her buyers was BELOW every lead who had never ordered, because Postgres sorts `DESC` nulls-first ([322]). Following the buyers it surfaced led to [323]. So: fast, and until today pointed at the wrong end of her list.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Growth board                 | **Done, and this is where P03 differs from P01.** P01 recorded it as `not checked` because there was no system tenant to write to; there is one now, and Devi's signup landed properly. Under the `wizeworks` tenant: contact `960fe725` (`p03.devi@piggles.test`), deal `d708cb12` (`Juniper Row (juniper-row)`), source `signup`, stage Trial, trial ending Sep 6, acquisition `marketing-site` / `pricing-hero`, and her Piggles rail answer `[web, sell, people]` carried through. The tag is **`brand-piggles`**, not `brand:piggles` as this file and the other nine persona files say — `toTag` rewrites the colon because the tag column rejects one, so the docs are the stale half, not the code. The **story fields were all null**, for every Piggles tenant AND every sparx tenant in the database, which is [320] — fixed, and the trade now reaches the board.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Usage rollup                 | **Done — reads sensibly, and handles what it has not measured correctly.** On getpiggles › Your account, _What you are using_: **People on your team 1**, **Websites 5** (Juniper Row, Archive, Journal, Press, Trade — exactly her five), **Locations 2**, and then **Customers**, **Photos and files** and **Messages sent this month** all reading **"Not measured yet"** above the line _"Your first overnight count has not run yet, so some of these are still blank."_ That is the right answer rather than a missing one: `/v1/usage/capacity` preserves `null` deliberately — its own comment says a zero "would be read as a measurement" — and the screen says so in her words. **Two counts worth knowing rather than filing:** "Locations 2" counts STOCK locations, and both of Devi's (`Main Warehouse`, `Fulfillment Center`) were created by setup rather than by her — a one-person studio with no shop was given a fulfilment centre it did not ask for. And no meter shows a ceiling or an over state, which matches the page saying plainly that "adding a payment method, seeing invoices, and buying more room are the next thing being built". **Also confirmed [316] from the owner's side here:** _Your business address_ reads **`juniper-row.piggles.site`**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

| [461](issues/461-two-bills-due-the-same-day-one-late-one-not.md)                                                  | major    | Two bills due the same day, one late and one not                                                         | fixed                             | Eight invoices printed "Due Sep 8, 2026". Seven read "1 day late" and one read "Not yet due", with $234.60 sitting in the wrong aging bucket, because lateness was elapsed milliseconds: INV-000001 was raised at noon so only 0.93 of a 24-hour period had passed, while INV-000004 was raised at 02:41 and had 1.31. The due date a shop READS is formatted as a UTC calendar day on purpose (formatDay: "the day it actually is"), so the date and the verdict were computed on two different bases and the label was decided by a time she was never shown. FIVE separate copies of "how late is this bill" existed -- bucketAging, the receivables route's own copy, the dunning ladder's exact-day overdueDays predicate, the B2B credit-hold ladder, and a raw SQL scan -- plus deriveDocumentStatus deciding whether a document IS overdue. All six now call one exported daysPastDue counting calendar days in UTC, the same basis the date is displayed in. The dunning consequence was the sharper one: matching overdueDays == 7/14/30 exactly meant the day a customer got chased was set by the hour the invoice happened to be raised at. The existing tests built every due date from a midnight NOW, where both rules agree for every input, so the wrong implementation passed all of them -- the new cases use real due times (02:41, 12:00, 23:59) and reddening the rule fails exactly 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

A green toast said "Cost recorded", the status bar said "Saved just now", and the list underneath said "$0.00 / 0 costs / Nothing recorded yet". Refresh changed nothing; the row was in the database, correct in every field. The list asks for ?from=2026-09-01&to=2026-09-09 and the server filtered incurredAt lte a coerced midnight, so a range ending TODAY contained none of today -- every cost recorded today invisible until tomorrow, on the screen that records them, with re-typing it the obvious next move. The period picker that builds the range states the contract the server broke: "Ranges are calendar-boundary DATES (YYYY-MM-DD), not instants." Two more places carried the same bound: the accounting export (so the last day of every period sent to an accountant was short) and markExported, which must cover exactly the rows the export sent or the last day goes unstamped and is offered again as still-needs-sending. A shared endOfDayExclusive now names the rule, built on utcDayRange, whose own comment already called the half-open range "the range every query below uses". Two bucket-column filters were deliberately left alone (a DAY column's stored values ARE midnights), and finance/channels.ts looked identical until I checked its client sends an instant -- changed, then reverted. Proven on screen; a second cost then appeared with no refresh, so cache invalidation had been working the whole time and the date bound was the entire defect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

The screen had no way to say so: its refresh control showed dataUpdatedAt, react-query's timestamp for when the BROWSER last fetched, so a page opened at 5pm read "updated just now" over numbers computed at 06:45. A freshness marker measuring the wrong thing is worse than none -- it answers the question a shop is actually asking, wrongly, with confidence. rollup_finance_daily_profit.computed_at has been written on every rebuild since it shipped and read by nobody; profitForRange now returns the newest one across the range (null when nothing has ever been worked out) and the control shows THAT. Proven: rebuilt at 10:43, reloaded at 10:51, marker reads "8 minutes ago" where it would have said "just now". I first thought computedAt was the fix for the $0.00 revenue and it is NOT -- the rollup had been recomputed seconds earlier by the cost she recorded, so it would have said "just now" and still shown zero; I reverted it, found the real cause, and re-added it for the reason it actually serves. REAL CAUSE, left for Brandon because it costs money: recomputeDay reads revenue from a rollup only the nightly cron maintains, and while the Rebuild BUTTON reconciles revenue first (its comment explains exactly why), the event path triggered by recording a cost does not. Closing it needs either a reconcile on the read path or a new consumer keeping the revenue rollup fresh -- both recurring database work                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [464](issues/464-a-screen-that-answered-500-because-a-query-named-a-field-that-does-not-exist.md)                 | blocker  | "By job" answered 500 for every shop, and TypeScript could not see it                                    | fixed                             | The pane sat on "Just a moment..." for twenty-five seconds and then gave up. Every request it makes in its DEFAULT filter answered 500: types=order returned 200, types=booking and the bare default returned 500, so the screen had never worked on first open for anybody since it shipped. jobProfitability asked a booking for its `customer`, and Booking has NO such relation, deliberately -- 78-scheduling.prisma keeps scheduling unaware that CRM exists, so a booking carries a bare customerId with nothing to join, exactly as it does for meetingLinkId. The part that matters more than the bug: TypeScript DOES NOT CHECK THE CONTENTS OF A PRISMA SELECT. Measured on a file that typechecks clean -- `where: { notAColumn: true }` is TS2353, `select: { customer: {...} }` compiles. A generated <Model>Select is $Extensions.GetSelect<...>, a mapped type over a TYPE PARAMETER, and excess-property checking only runs against a resolved key set; `where` has no such wrapper, which is what makes the gap invisible. I proved tsc covers the file first by breaking something else in the same function. A new check:prisma-selects reads the field list from prisma/schema/*.prisma (in-repo, so no generate needed) and validates every select and include key with the TypeScript parser, descending through relations: 6,213 fields across 422 models, SIX wrong across four files. Two are worse than this one -- Ticket.resolveDueAt/respondDueAt (really resolutionDueAt/firstResponseDueAt) threw before the resolver read a single field, so every automation keyed on a ticket has been dead; and ProductVariant.isAvailable + Product.currency + Order.email threw whenever an offer was picked, so both halves of the offer stack never showed anything. Wired into pre-push and CI; reinstating the booking select reddens 1 and moves the denominator 6217 to 6218; renaming a scan root throws rather than scanning nothing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

The Spending quick-add is three fields and a button on purpose (its own comment: "a person entering a shoebox of receipts") and writes paidAt: null, dueAt: null, which is the honest record of what she said: a cost happened. It says nothing about whether the money left. This screen read that absence as a debt and summed every such row into the headline. The file header already knew about the receipt someone types in -- "LATENESS IS COMPUTED FROM dueAt AND NOTHING ELSE. A cost with no due date is not late, it is simply unpaid" -- and stopped one clause short: it guarded the lateness and counted the row as owed anyway. Two related bounds moved with it: no_date is out of the aging BAR entirely, and "Coming up" no longer includes dateless rows because nothing is coming. | [466](issues/466-thirty-sentences-speaking-the-other-products-language.md)                                        | major    | Thirty sentences still speaking the other product's language                                             | fixed                             | The payouts tab is renamed to "Money paid to you" because payouts is the accountant's word; the screen inside it said "No payouts yet". check:piggles-nav exists to stop exactly this and was green, because all four of its seams read a string that passes through SOMETHING -- a catalog entry, a copy key, a title slot -- and a sentence typed straight into JSX passes through nothing. Thirty were live: the command palette said "Type to search across every module", Add a site (which Devi has used seven times) said "needs the Builder module", filing a product spent fourteen sentences teaching the word "collection" that piggles/CLAUDE.md RULE #3 names outright as one a person must never be made to learn, choosing photos five more, plus CRM in a leave-guard and a toolbar label, "the customers module", "the scheduling module", and "build headless against our API" on a first-run screen. The sharpest is on the very surface seam 4 was written for: act 115 removed setTitle("How the CRM behaves") from the customer-settings pane and the leave-guard FIVE LINES BELOW went on asking whether to discard "your changes to how the CRM behaves". A fifth seam reads JSX text nodes, the props that render text, and whole sentences in string literals -- the last because the palette placeholder lives in a ternary, which is neither of the first two and is read by everyone who presses the shortcut. 624 rendered strings before, 12,335 now. Deliberately narrow (class lists, copy keys and productCopy fallbacks excluded) because a checker that flags className="bg-module" gets switched off. Two kinds of exemption, both self-destructing: the marketplace card and the sparx Pay form are keyed on their hiddenFeatures entry and the check THROWS if either stops being hidden, and three terms a person must meet because somebody else's screen says them (API key, webhook signing secret, and one automation that defines the word in the same sentence) are exact strings, so a new sentence carrying the same word is still caught. The replacements use words Piggles already had and had not applied to its prose: a group of products, an app, the Customers app; media collections had no word and are now albums                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [467](issues/467-a-500-that-told-her-to-check-her-internet.md)                                                    | major    | A 500 that told her to check her internet                                                                | fixed                             | After about twenty-five seconds of retrying a request that answered 500, the pane said "The server could not be reached. Nothing you have recorded is affected." The server WAS reached -- it answered in 57 milliseconds, and its answer was that it had failed. A shop owner reading that goes and looks at her internet, then her router, then rings somebody, and none of it can help. This is issue 286 one cause later: that split "this record is gone" (404) out of "could not be reached", and a 5xx is the THIRD cause still wearing the first one's sentence -- one outcome covering two causes whose remedies differ. paneLoadReason now returns missing / failed / unreachable, and the sentence for the new state is owned by the COMPONENT rather than the call site, for the same reason the "gone" sentence already is: every caller's own description is written about the unreachable case, so a 5xx wearing it is wrong in a hundred places at once and one edit reaches all of them with no call site changed. Retry stays offered because some 5xx are momentary; only the claim about the connection goes. Removing the branch reddens 2 with "expected unreachable to be failed". MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FILED: while the failing request retried, the pane showed the PREVIOUS filter's rows -- Appointments listing two orders under a highlighted Appointments chip for about twenty seconds. Measured with the real library rather than guessed: during a failing fetch react-query reports status success, isError false, isPlaceholderData TRUE and the old data; after it gives up, status error and data undefined. None of the 155 call sites using placeholderData for a question change reads that flag. Not filed as 155 defects: keeping the last answer while the next loads is deliberate and generally right, the refresh control already reads as busy throughout, and at normal speed the window is a few hundred milliseconds. What made it harmful was a request that could never succeed, which 464 fixed. Recorded because it names the mechanism and the unread flag if a second screen is ever seen doing it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [468](issues/468-two-categories-one-name.md)                                                                      | major    | Two categories with the same name, and no way to tell them apart                                         | fixed                             | Devi added "Packaging & gift wrap" for her boutique, then added it again, and the server answered 201 Created. The second copy landed in Running costs because the kind dropdown resets to its default and she had not touched it, so the SAME NAME sat on both sides of the gross-profit line -- and the picker where a cost is actually filed showed two identical lines with nothing to choose between them, on a screen whose own closing paragraph says filing a cost in the wrong group changes whether a job looks worth doing. The table HAS a unique index and it is on (tenant_id, slug); a tenant-invented category has NO slug, correctly and deliberately, because the slug namespace belongs to the seeded set derivers address and a tenant minting `wages` would collide with it. Postgres treats NULLs as distinct, so that index says nothing whatsoever about invented rows and the NAME was guarded by nothing -- not the database, not createCategory, not updateCategory. This module guards everything else with a typed error and a sentence an owner can act on: a seeded category cannot be deleted, one with spend behind it cannot be deleted, changing a kind warns that past profit figures will move. Uniqueness is the one nobody wrote, and the index beside it looks like it covers this. Renaming was worse than creating: nothing stopped renaming an invented category to "Rent", leaving two rows called Rent of which only one is findable by slug. One assertNameFree now serves both writers, inside the caller transaction so it cannot race a second create, case and space insensitive because "rent" and "Rent " are the same word to the person typing them, storing the trimmed name for the same reason. It checks ARCHIVED rows too, which gives the error two forms because the remedies differ -- a live clash wants a different name, an archived one wants bringing back, and saying "you already have one" about a row not on her screen sends her hunting for something she cannot see. CATEGORY_NAME_TAKEN is a 409 beside the two category conflicts already there. Proven by typing lowercase "rent" and getting the sentence back naming the existing category with ITS capitalization; removing the create guard reddens 4, the rename guard 1, the trim 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [469](issues/469-every-warning-a-download-carried-had-never-been-shown.md)                                        | blocker  | Every warning a download carried had never once been shown                                               | fixed                             | A cross-origin fetch can read exactly seven response headers -- Cache-Control, Content-Language, Content-Length, Content-Type, Expires, Last-Modified, Pragma -- and nothing else unless the server names it in Access-Control-Expose-Headers. api-rest set no exposedHeaders at all. Measured in the browser on the console own origin, [...response.headers.keys()] answers ["content-length","content-type"]. There is no error, no console warning and no failed request: headers.get() simply answers null and every caller fallback beside it turns that into an answer. Three shipped that way in BOTH consoles for as long as the endpoints have existed. content-disposition unreadable, so every accounting export saved as expenses.csv and every timesheet as hours.csv -- August and September collide in a Downloads folder with no way to tell them apart. x-sparx-skipped-rows unreadable, so the accounting export always said "Every cost in that period is in the file" and its rows-left-out warning never fired. And x-sparx-unpriced-minutes unreadable, so the timesheet export sentence -- "12h 30m are in the hours column but not the cost column: nobody has a pay rate covering them. They still have to be paid" -- HAS NEVER APPEARED, not once, for anybody, on a file somebody pays staff from. Both routes carry a careful comment about why the fact rides on a header ("a download cannot carry a warning", "the discrepancy somebody will otherwise spend an afternoon hunting") and both authors were defeated by one missing line of configuration four hundred files away. Found only because a fix to the export toast changed nothing on screen and I asked why rather than assuming a stale dev server. Fixed with an explicit allowlist in api-rest/src/lib/exposed-headers.ts carrying the reason above it, handed to @fastify/cors beside the methods array that is there for the same kind of silent default; explicit rather than * so adding one is a decision. New check:exposed-headers reads that allowlist, scans both consoles surfaces/ and lib/ for headers.get(), requires every non-safelisted name to be on it, and ALSO asserts app.ts actually passes the list to CORS -- a perfect allowlist nobody registers is the same bug wearing a tidier hat. Next route handlers under app/api/** read REQUEST headers and are deliberately out of scope, because a check with false positives gets switched off. Reports 10 reads across 1997 client files. Its first version had the bug it exists to catch: an apostrophe in the prose above an entry paired with the next one and swallowed a real header, so it strips comments first and now refuses anything that does not parse as a header name. Dropping one header reddens 2, removing exposedHeaders throws, renaming a scan root throws. Wired into pre-push and CI |
| [470](issues/470-every-cost-is-in-the-file-said-over-an-empty-file.md)                                            | major    | "Every cost in that period is in the file", said over an empty file                                      | fixed                             | The accounting export period defaults to Last month. Devi opened it on the 9th, so the range was Aug 1 to Aug 31 and she has no costs in August -- her two are dated the 9th. Nothing on the screen said so. Download the file, with "Mark these as sent" ticked by default, answered "Every cost in that period is in the file." That sentence is TRUE of a period with nothing in it, because a period with nothing in it has all of its nothing in there, and it is also the exact sentence somebody needs to read to believe August is filed with their accountant -- the file that would say otherwise has to be opened in a spreadsheet to find out. Two outcomes were coded, some rows skipped or none, and the "none" branch was written about a full file; an empty file is a third outcome wearing the first one words. Fixed in two places. BEFORE, which prevents it: the date range now carries a count -- "Aug 1, 2026 to Aug 31, 2026 - no costs recorded", "Sep 1, 2026 to Sep 9, 2026 - 2 costs" -- because the dates alone do not answer the question somebody is actually asking, which is whether this file will have their spending in it. Counting was free: listExpenses already runs an aggregate for totalCents, so it returns totalCount off the same query and the export card asks for one row to read it. totalCount describes the FILTER not the page, same grain as totalCents beside it, because a page-shaped count would tell somebody a period holds a single cost when it holds fifty. AFTER, which reports it honestly: three outcomes, with the empty one a warning naming the range and telling her to change the period. That needed the server to say how many rows it wrote -- it already knew, rowCount goes into the sync-run record and the completion event -- so it rides on x-sparx-row-count, which was itself unreadable until 469; the first version of this fix changed nothing on screen and that is how 469 was found. The client reads a MISSING header as -1 rather than 0, because a server that has said nothing about the row count has not said zero, and reporting it as "no costs" would invent the very claim this exists to stop. Counting rows.length instead of the aggregate reddens the page-size test that already existed for totalCents                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

The six rows inside it all say below -- QuickBooks Online, Xero, QuickBooks Desktop, Sage 50, FreshBooks and Wave, each telling her to use the spreadsheet export below. There is nothing below; the export card is the second thing on the screen, so somebody following the instruction scrolls to the bottom and finds the end of the page. The sentences are written in @wizeworks/finance and the console decides where the export card sits, so a package cannot know which way to point and "below" was a guess that happened to be wrong. Three files carry it (the shared accountingCatalog builder plus the QuickBooks and Xero adapters, which each write their own) and each now carries a comment saying why there is no direction word, so nobody puts one back. ## Act 127 — Ashcombe invoiced two metres, and the console called it a disagreement

Ashcombe Mills sent two replacement metres for the water-stained ones and billed
for those two. Devi entered the invoice exactly as it reads: 2 at $18.00.

> **$36.00** · The check: **1 line(s) do not agree** · **$684.00 in your favour**
>
> Linen, natural, 200gsm · ordered 40 · arrived 40 · **billed 2** ·
> **Billed for less than arrived · $684.00**
>
> **Before this can be approved.** Either accept the difference, which is
> recorded against your name, or query it with the supplier.

The invoice is right. The price agrees. Her order arrived in two drops, 38 then
2, and the second one was invoiced on its own, which is how every shop that
takes a part-delivery works. The check compared it against the whole order, so
every invoice but the last reads short
([510](issues/510-a-partial-invoice-reads-as-a-disagreement.md)).

Measured before touching anything: `GR-000001` 38 units, `GR-000002` 2 units,
one bill covering 2. The other 38 metres are simply not invoiced yet.

**The blindness ran the other way too, and that half costs money.** Because
nothing in the check ever looked at the other invoices, a supplier who invoiced
the same drop twice matched perfectly, both times. Neither invoice on its own
exceeds what arrived.

And a third, found only while writing the test for the second: quantity was
decided before price, so a partial invoice that also OVERCHARGED reported the
shortfall and never mentioned the money. Harmless while a shortfall blocked the
bill. Fatal the moment it stopped.

So the check now counts the other invoices, tests money before shortfalls, and
reports a shortfall instead of disputing it. Proven three ways on the screen:
her real invoice agrees and says "$684.00 of this order is still to be
invoiced"; the 38-metre drop entered as AM-2198 agrees and shows "2 on other
invoices"; the same drop entered a second time is caught as **$684.00 more than
the goods justify**, which the old code could not have seen at all.

### The screen she was left on after querying it

She queried the duplicate, which is exactly right, and landed on a pane that had
forgotten she had done anything:

> **Before this can be approved** · Why _[empty]_ ·
> **An override that leaves no trace looks exactly like nobody noticing.**
> [Accept the difference] [Query it with them]

Her reason was in the database and on no screen. The pane measured 908 of 908,
so nothing was scrolled away. Accepting a difference has always displayed its
reason in an alert; querying had no equivalent
([511](issues/511-querying-an-invoice-was-a-one-way-door.md)).

Two worse things sat behind it. **Querying was a one-way door.** Approve refuses
on a disputed bill, paying refuses on a disputed bill, and the only remaining
transition is cancel. The ordinary ending of a query had nowhere to go. And the
other button was a trap: accepting from a queried bill would have written over
the query's reason, stamped the variance accepted, left the status disputed, and
stranded the invoice.

Fixed: the reason shows, the card knows what she did, accepting is refused while
it is out with them, and **The query is settled** returns it to a draft.

### One I wrote myself, twice in one sentence

The settle card's first version said the figures "can be put right off their new
paper", with two em-dashes in it. Both wrong. The em-dashes are against a
standing rule about this product's voice. And no such thing is possible:
`UpdateSupplierBillInput` takes number, dates, tax, freight and notes and **no
lines**.

That turned out to be correct rather than a gap, and for the reason
[509](issues/509-the-console-accused-her-supplier-of-overcharging.md) already
named: a supplier's invoice is a copy of a piece of paper. A corrected invoice
is a different piece of paper with a different number. So the sentence was
rewritten to the three endings that actually exist (cancel and enter theirs, or
settle and accept), and the promise matches the product.

| issue                                                          | severity | what                                                                                                                              | status           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| [510](issues/510-a-partial-invoice-reads-as-a-disagreement.md) | major    | A correct partial invoice read as a disagreement, a duplicate invoice matched perfectly, and an overcharge hid behind a shortfall | fixed and proven |
| [511](issues/511-querying-an-invoice-was-a-one-way-door.md)    | major    | Querying an invoice left no trace on screen, offered the same two choices again, and had no way back                              | fixed and proven |

### And one my own fix caused

With the duplicate queried, the CORRECT invoice on that order turned red:

> AM-2214 · **1 line(s) do not agree** · $36.00 more than the goods justify
> arrived 40 · **76 on other invoices** · billed 2

The new sum of other invoices excluded cancelled bills and not queried ones, so
a bill she had just refused to pay was still consuming the quantity it charged
for. Disputing the duplicate turned the one honest invoice into a finding, which
is the opposite of what disputing it is for. A bill nobody is going to pay as it
stands consumes nothing. AM-2214 now reads **38 on other invoices · Agrees**.

Every test was green when that shipped, both consoles typechecked, both linted,
and the parity check passed. What found it was opening the other invoice and
looking at it.

## Act 128 — Putting a form back the way she found it

She had already seen this one and it had been written off as too big to touch.
With the schedule back to exactly what the server held, the status bar still
read **"Not saved: a panel"**, and closing it would still have asked her to
confirm discarding changes she had undone.

The issue as filed said this was the house pattern across roughly 120 panes and
needed a considered replacement. Counted rather than asserted:

```
panes declaring unsaved work : 122
  already compare a draft    :  72
  sticky boolean             :   6
  other shapes               :  44
```

**The house already did it right.** Six panes were the stragglers, and the fix
was not a new mechanism but bringing them back to the one in use next door. The
scope note was the only thing standing in the way, and it was wrong.

All six converted, in both consoles. Proven on screen twice: the counting
schedule goes clean when the zone box is emptied again, and on INV-000010 the
Save button goes back to grey and **Send again** comes back the moment two typed
characters are backspaced.

Three of them cleared the flag before closing themselves, which turned out never
to have mattered. The controller says so in its own words: a surface closing
ITSELF goes through `close()`, which deletes the guards first, "prompting
'unsaved changes?' about a document that no longer exists would be nonsense".
Those lines were removed rather than replaced.

### The patch that would not apply

The same change went into both consoles' invoice editors and failed in sparx, on
a block Piggles had already rewritten. The typecheck error was the whole story:

```
invoice-editor.tsx(174,18): Property 'notes' does not exist on type 'BillingDocument'
```

Sparx seeded its notes box from a hardcoded `''` and its save sends
`notes || null` over whatever is stored. So on sparx, **a note written on an
invoice disappears the moment the pane reloads and is deleted from the record on
the next save**, with success reported both times. That note is the text the
customer reads on the document itself. Piggles fixed this and left a comment
saying exactly that; the neighbour was never brought along
([512](issues/512-the-sparx-invoice-editor-wiped-the-note-on-every-save.md)).

The console's own type simply had a hole where the field should be, which is why
nothing ever complained.

Fixed. And the same comparison turned up a second gap that is not fixed: sparx
can SHOW that an invoice is overdue and has no way to SET when it is due. Filed
rather than ported blind, because the piggles version carries a date rule that
is wrong by one day if it is copied carelessly.

## Act 129 — The search box learns what a warehouse calls things

Devi holds a delivery note and types the number on it. Until today the answer
was a list of SCREENS whose words happened to contain the same letters, because
the universal index carried twenty kinds of record and not one of them came from
purchasing.

Seven projectors later, typing one supplier's name returns her whole file with
them:

> **Suppliers** — Ashcombe Mills · ASHCOMBE
> **Customers** — Wren Ashcombe
> **Supplier invoices** — AM-2231, AM-2198, AM-2214 · all Ashcombe Mills
> **Deliveries** — GR-000002, GR-000001 · Ashcombe Mills
> **Orders to suppliers** — PO-000001 · Ashcombe Mills
> **Gift cards** — QM44-2DTN-6HM4-6RA9 · Nadia Ashcombe
>
> 9 records matched. The rest are screens.

Not one of those invoices or deliveries matched on its own number. They matched
on the supplier's NAME, because a delivery is looked for by who sent it at least
as often as by what it is called, so every document carries the numbers and
names around it ([508](issues/508-search-everything-cannot-find-a-purchase-order.md)).

Clicking GR-000001 opened the delivery.

### The half that matters more than the projectors

A projector makes yesterday's record findable after a rebuild. It does nothing
for the order she raises this afternoon, and an index that is right only just
after a rebuild looks exactly like a working one until somebody searches for
what they just made.

So every write signals, through `afterCommit` — the mechanism that already fires
on commit and is discarded on rollback, so nothing announces an order that was
undone. Proven the hard way: the first version missed the expected-date change
entirely, because that goes through `/reschedule` rather than the update
endpoint. Found by doing it on screen and watching nothing arrive.

Two more a blind sweep would have got wrong. The approvals file shares one
`audit()` helper whose callers pass an approval RULE id under the order's entity
type three times out of five, so the call went on the two real order sites
instead. And booking a delivery in moves the ORDER's status, so re-projecting
only the receipt would leave the order calling itself outstanding until somebody
edited it again.

### And the thing I had been wrong about all session

The local index held 20 documents across 113 tenants, and I had written that
down as "`sparx-nats` is unhealthy, so indexing is dead". Both halves were
wrong. The broker was fine; its HEALTHCHECK was broken, using a bash feature the
image's `sh` does not have, failing 1,355 times in a row since the day it was
written. Asked directly, NATS reported JetStream up, 1,050 API calls and zero
errors, with the indexer having consumed 9,526 messages and none pending.

The index was empty because nothing had ever backfilled it. Every document in it
was an integration-test fixture.

A container's health LABEL is not the container's health, which is the same
lesson as a 200 not being a working page, and I had carried the wrong diagnosis
forward for a whole session on the strength of one word
([513](issues/513-sparx-could-not-tell-you-its-storefront-was-invisible.md)).

The Piggles console handles this properly and says so on the products list:
"Searching your shop won't find 31 of your products", with a button. Pressing it
took the index from 20 documents to 359 and the palette started finding real
products. **Sparx had none of that** — no status read, no notice, no rebuild —
while running the same api-rest, the same worker and the same Typesense. Ported,
and proven both ways: the notice appeared over 107 unfindable products and
disappeared once the rebuild landed.

| [508](issues/508-search-everything-cannot-find-a-purchase-order.md)        | major    | Nothing in purchasing was searchable by the numbers a warehouse actually uses | fixed and proven |
| [513](issues/513-sparx-could-not-tell-you-its-storefront-was-invisible.md) | major    | sparx could not tell you its storefront was invisible, or rebuild the index   | fixed and proven |

## Act 130 — Nine and a half thousand sentences, and the dash that stays

The house rule is that copy never carries an em-dash. It had been followed for
new copy and never applied backwards. Measured before starting, counting only
text a person actually reads and never a comment: **about 9,500 across the
consoles, both marketing sites, the account app, the staff console, the shared
packages and the services.**

About **7,800 sentences** were rewritten. A dash is not one thing, so one
replacement was never going to work: two whole sentences take a full stop, a
label and the thing it names takes a colon, two halves of one sentence take a
comma, and a short fenced aside takes brackets. Every proposal was read before it
was applied, and the machine refused on anything it could not place. Roughly 900
of those refusals were written out one at a time.

**Seven rules had to be corrected, and every one was caught by reading rather
than by a test.** The worst was a fence rule that treated two dashes in a
paragraph as one aside and bracketed everything between them, which turned the
Builder pitch into "in front of your work (themes, pages, a custom domain, all
handled. Pick a theme, edit it, publish. The same builder serves a portfolio, a
blog, or a 50,000-product catalog) selling is optional." Six paragraphs went out
like that before it was spotted. The second worst flattened a multi-line markdown
document onto one line, because the rewrite table is keyed on the collapsed body
of a string and writing that back destroys the line breaks, which ARE the
content. Eight files were restored and redone with an applier that refuses to
touch a region containing a line break.

**The bare `—` that means "no value" stays, all 581 of them.** It is not prose
with a dash in it, it is a glyph standing in for a figure nobody measured, and
the product explains itself in exactly those words on the page-results screen:
"That is why Bought and Sales read `—` rather than zero: nothing was measured, so
there is nothing to report." Swapping it would contradict a sentence we ship.
Test names stay too, for the same reason the 7,000 dashes in `//` comments stay:
the rule is about the words a customer reads.

Three tests went red and each is worth keeping. One asserts copy through a
**regular expression**, which an AST walk over string literals cannot see. One
builds its own line as `${rule} — ${evidence}` and then filters for that exact
shape, so the shared chunk was swept and the filter, which exists only in that
file, was not: **its count went from 56 to 0 and it went red rather than passing
over nothing**, which is what that check was written to do. One asserts the
output a merge-tag template renders to, where neither half matches the source.

Reading 7,800 sentences turned up something else. **436 of them are written in
British English**, against a rule that is just as old. Four were fixed, including
an "in your favour" I put on the supplier bill screen earlier this same session.
The rest is filed as its own pass, because `cancelled` is 175 of the 436 and is
also a stored status on orders, bookings, subscriptions and purchase orders: a
blind replace would rename data.

| issue                                                       | severity | what                                                             | status            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| [514](issues/514-the-em-dash-sweep.md)                      | minor    | 7,800 sentences carried the tell the house rule exists to remove | done              |
| [515](issues/515-the-copy-is-written-in-british-english.md) | minor    | 436 sentences are written in British English                     | measured, 4 fixed |

## Act 131 — The dash that was spelled out, and the copy that is not in any file

The source sweep was finished, green on every check, and written up as done. Then
the Piggles home page was opened, and the first paragraph carried an em-dash.

It was spelled `&mdash;`. The scan reads string literals and looks for the
CHARACTER, and an entity is six ASCII letters, so **fourteen sentences on live
marketing pages sat through the whole sweep untouched.** Also checked and clear:
`&#8212;`, `&#x2014;`, and `—` escapes.

That one sentence opened two more surfaces, neither of them in a file.

**Copy that ships as ROWS.** The banner reading "for as long as they stay — ask
us how" is not in any `.ts`. It is a row in `platform_announcements`, written by
a migration. Measured across the whole database: **5,421 rows in 79 columns**
carry a dash. Almost all of it is a stale copy of source this sweep already
fixed, and every seed source now measures zero, so a fresh seed carries the
corrected text. The banner is the exception, because only a migration can change
what a migration wrote.

**The blueprint catalog.** 191 of 191 bundles, **8,408 dashes in shipped starter
content and 9,248 in the generators**, in copy that is COPIED into a tenant's
site at install. Brandon's call, because the fix is outward-facing: a content
change with no version bump reaches nobody, and a bump offers an update to every
tenant who installed one.

**A regen was not available.** The template generators assign node ids from a
random base, so running one rewrites every id in its `site.json`, and those ids
are persisted and used as React and dnd keys. So the generator and the JSON it
emitted were edited in lockstep and no generator was run. Both halves run through
ONE decision function, because the catalog holds each sentence twice and the two
must not drift.

**13,504 replacements across 880 JSON files and 364 generators.** Proven: zero
files where added lines differ from removed, **zero changed lines touching an
`id`, `nodeId` or `key`**, and all 1,136 JSON files still parse. The JSON was
spliced as text rather than re-serialized, because a round-trip is not
byte-identical and would have reformatted every file.

Then **191 version bumps in four places each**: the bundle's `sparx.json`, its
`blueprint.ts` (the loader cross-checks the pair), the shared harness
`BUNDLE_VERSION`, and two standalone generators. Miss either of the last two and
the next regen quietly puts the old number back.

The rules needed two more corrections, both found by reading. A sign-off,
"Back in a fortnight. — Iris", came out as "fortnight., Iris": no mark belongs
after a full stop. And a product spec, "Enamel Mug — 12oz speckled camp mug", was
being refused because the right half opens with a figure, which is never a
sentence and always the thing being described.

**Reading the diff is not reading the screen.** Everything above was found by
opening a page, not by scanning source.

## Act 132 — the sweep almost emailed every customer twice

With the console back up I went looking at what my own sweep had changed, and
found that the dangerous part was never the words. It was **what reads them**.

An idempotent installer has to know whether it has already put a thing in an
account. Three of them decide that by matching a sentence a person reads. The
worst is the system-automation seeder, matched on `(origin='system', name)` and
driven **daily across every tenant** by the reconcile pass. I had reworded 32 of
those names, thirty of which send an email.

A renamed seed does not update the old row. It misses, and a miss is
indistinguishable from "never installed", so it installs a second copy. Nothing
errors and nothing is marked. Every tenant would have ended up with two active
copies of order confirmation, shipping confirmation, delivered, cancelled,
refunded, payment failed, every subscription notice and the whole dunning ladder,
and every customer would have received each of them twice.

Every check was green. A renamed string is a valid string.

The fix is not a rename migration, which would have bought this release and left
the next one to fall in. Seeds now declare `previousNames`, and the installer
**adopts and renames** the row it finds under a former name. Proven by
measurement rather than by reading: every `origin='system'` name in the database
against source, `current 56, former 32, db 56, unmatched 0`. Three tests, each
proven red by removing what it guards; the adoption one fails with `expected
[…] to have a length of 1 but got 2`, which is the defect stated as a number.

**"109 of 109 tasks pass" was a CI-mode run.** The pre-push guard sets
`CI=true`, which excludes the DB-backed integration suites, and two stale things
were sitting in them unseen: a test asserting copy that had legitimately changed,
and a fixture whose `+12h` nudge was written for arithmetic that had since moved
to calendar days, so the suite passed all morning and failed all evening.

Then I pressed **Rescan the site** on Get Found, as Devi would, and the screen
listed every check twice: "Title length, 33 of 37" directly above "How long the
title is, 52 of 93". A scorecard stores the words the checks had on the day that
page was scored, so a site holds several versions of the rules at once, and the
roll-up grouped on the words. Thirteen checks, twenty-six rows, four different
denominators. Grouping on the `id` and taking the newest wording put it back to
thirteen rows, all plain English, all counting 96 pages. That one was not mine;
it had been on screen since the plain-English pass.

Checking that my own fix had not duplicated anything found the same ending
arriving by a second door: two "Handle form submissions" rows on one tenant,
created a millisecond apart on 2026-07-14. `upsertSystemAutomation` is
check-then-insert with nothing underneath it. There is now a partial unique index
over the seeded rows, and the service re-reads the winner instead of throwing.

And the three migrations I wrote for all this would have done **nothing** in
production. Every table they touch is FORCE RLS and `sparx_owner` is a
non-superuser there, so an un-scoped `UPDATE` sees zero rows while passing
locally as superuser. All three now loop tenants with `set_config`, which is what
`packages/db/CLAUDE.md` has said all along and what I had not read closely enough
the first time.

## Act 133 — the dark site asked to be deleted rather than to be waited for

With the stack back up I finally opened my own shop the way a customer would.
The overlay is right: "Back soon. This site is taking a short break." Neutral,
kind, no mention of a bill. That part has been right since Act 130.

Then I looked at what the same pages say to a search engine, because a shop that
comes back to no listings has not really come back.

```
/robots.txt     200  User-agent: *  Disallow: /   max-age=300
/sitemap.xml    404
/llms.txt       404
/               200  Temporarily unavailable   noindex, nofollow
```

Four answers, and **every one of them means "remove me"**. None of them means
"wait", which is the only true thing about a shop whose card expired on Sunday.

Worse, the two guards cancel each other out. A crawler reads `robots.txt` first;
`Disallow: /` is a rule it stores and obeys, so from that moment it stops
fetching the pages, and it therefore never sees the `noindex` those pages carry.
The page guard only ever reached crawlers that had already ignored the disallow,
and the moment it reached one it asked for the listing to be dropped. Both
halves of the damage, neither half of the protection.

`noindex` is the instruction to REMOVE a URL from search. It is right for a page
that should not be listed and wrong for a page that will be listed again on
Thursday. And 404 does not say "ask again later" either, whatever the comment in
`lib/suspended.ts` claimed it said; 404 says there is nothing at this address.

There is one status that means ask again later, and none of the four was it.
Every dark answer is now **503 with `Retry-After: 600` and `no-store`**: the
crawler pauses, keeps what it already holds, and comes back. The neutral title
stays, so the blank page never sits in a result under Juniper Row's own name.

The page HTML still answers 200. A root layout cannot set a status in the App
Router, and the only way to move it puts a cache in front of the suspension
state, which would delay the lift after payment — and the console promises "it
comes back as soon as a payment goes through". That sentence is worth more than
the status code, and with `robots.txt` answering 503 the crawl is already paused
before any page is fetched.

**Fixing the shared file changed nothing on screen.** Every page still answered
`noindex, nofollow`, because `app/layout.tsx` held a SECOND copy of the same
decision written inline. Issue 503's own finding was that route metadata
overrides a layout's; the two copies agreeing was the only thing hiding it. Only
the measurement caught that. The diff looked complete and the tests were green.

Six guards, each proven red by putting the old behavior back: 6 failed, 6
passed, with `expected { index: false, follow: false } to be undefined` and
`expected 'user-agent: *\ndisallow: /\n' not to contain 'disallow'`.

Also, on Ashcombe Mills: the quantity price read "$18.00 each below the first
step" under a line saying "One price at every quantity." There is no first step.
It now reads "$18.00 each", and neither sentence is said at all until the ladder
has actually been read — an unread ladder is empty for the same reason a flat
price is, and only one of those has been measured.

| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| [518](issues/518-the-dark-site-asked-to-be-deleted-instead-of-waiting.md) | critical | A dark site sent `noindex` + `Disallow: /`; both mean remove, not wait | fixed  |

## Act 134 — half a product name, on 991 spans

Reading PO-000002 to Fairfield Trims. The Items table is good: the quantities
reconcile, the badge says "58 of 60", the banner above says "2 of 60 units still
to come". One thing on it is wrong and it is a thing that is not there.

```
Item            Qty   Cost each   Line total   Received
Brass belt h…    60      $3.60      $216.00     58 of 60
BRASS-BELT-1
```

**Brass belt h…** — and nothing reveals the rest. Not a hover, not a click. The
name needs 203px and has 101px, so exactly half of it is on screen, and the half
missing is the half that says which one it is.

Not one pane. **991 spans clip text across the two consoles, 352 of them showing
a name a person wrote, and not one of the 991 carried a `title`.** 45.6% of the
product titles on this platform are longer than the column that shows them. For
a clothing label it is the worst case, because the names differ at the END:
"Linen shirtdress, indigo" and "Linen shirtdress, oat" are the same string for
sixteen characters, so clipping them shows one row twice.

I did not fix it at 352 call sites. A sweep over JSX is the most expensive kind
of change to get wrong here — the one that deleted the filter chips from seven
lists passed typecheck, lint and 44 tests. And a blanket `title` on all 991
would be wrong more quietly: most of them are showing values that FIT, and a
tooltip repeating the line already on screen is how a tooltip stops meaning
anything.

So it is fixed once, as behavior, in `@wizeworks/app-kit`, whose own header says
nothing in it has an appearance, a variant, or a token. A native `title` has
none of those. One delegated listener measures the element under the pointer and
reveals it only if it is genuinely clipped. Nothing is measured until somebody
hovers.

An author's own `title` is never touched. A `title` this put there comes back
off the moment the element stops being clipped. One pixel of slack, because
sub-pixel layout rounds `scrollWidth` past `clientWidth` on lines nobody
clipped. And `line-clamp` counts: the part below the fold is just as unreachable
as the part past the right edge.

Seven guards, all seven proven red over two passes. On my own screen: clipped →
the whole name; widened until it fits → gone; narrowed back → returned; **42
spans on that page that FIT, none of them given a tooltip**; a span carrying the
author's own title, untouched.

## Act 135 — a box on my own counter would have said it was on the way

Filtering my orders by **Delivered** gives three, and all three are marked
**Collected**. That is right: my three finished orders were picked up in person,
and the badge asks each order which of the two it was, because issue 215 fixed
"Collected" being printed on things going in the post.

Looking at where that question gets asked found a branch where it does not.

`shippingState` has five branches and three of them can be reached by a
collection. Two of them ask:

| stored      | asks? | posted     | collected  |
| ----------- | ----- | ---------- | ---------- |
| `placed`    | yes   | To send    | To collect |
| `fulfilled` | NO    | On the way | On the way |
| `delivered` | yes   | Delivered  | Collected  |

`fulfilled` means everything is picked and packed. In the post that is with the
carrier. For a collection it is **on my own counter**. The console would have
said "On the way", and under it, the sentence you read when you stop:

> This order has been sent and is with the carrier.

Nothing had been sent. There is no carrier. I would have told somebody on the
phone their order was in transit about a box three feet away from me.

Nobody had seen it because nothing is in that state yet: 30 fulfilled orders
platform-wide and not one of them a collection. It is not unreachable though —
`pack-fulfillment` promotes any order once every item is packed and does not
care how the customer is getting it. The first shop to pack a collection before
the customer walks in gets the wrong sentence.

The comment above that very function says it is "the one place both the list and
the order pane read it from, so correcting it here corrects it everywhere rather
than in the two call sites that happened to notice". Exactly right, and it was
still corrected in two branches out of three. Both trees held their own copy of
the gap.

Ten guards now, **one per branch** rather than one for the case I found, because
a branch nobody tested is how this happened. Putting the defect back reddens
exactly two, and one of them is the sentence: `expected 'This order has been
sent and is with …' not to match /carrier|sent to|in transit/i`.

I left the chip bar alone and said why in the issue. It reads "Delivered" over
rows that read "Collected", and on every shop where that happens it is total
rather than partial — 3 of 3 here, 2 of 2 at Halo & Hem, 1 of 1 and 2 of 2 at
Quiet Haven. But a chip names a filter and a badge states a fact about one
order, and a collected order did reach the customer. Every covering word I tried
either lost the meaning that makes the chip useful or widened a bar the file
protects on purpose. That is a voice call with a real trade-off, not a defect.

## Act 136 — the rail marked an app it never scrolled to

The rail is the thing I look at every day, and on a laptop it shows 38% of
itself. Measured at 1280x800 on my own console: the list has **319px** to show
**848px** in. Thirteen apps plus Favourites and Recent, and once the header, the
plan card, the "Action needed" card and the footer have taken their share,
everything from **Sell** downwards is already clipped.

A scrolling list is fine. This is not:

A **pinned** panel reopens where it was left — `use-shell-prefs` restores
`state.module` on load — and the rail marks that app `aria-current`, with its
scroller at zero.

```
marked app        My Team
rail scrollTop    0
scroller          top 133 -> bottom 452
marked row        top 925 -> bottom 969      473px below the fold
marked visible    false
```

So I come back the next morning to a panel full of my team and a rail with no
selection anywhere I can see. Which is exactly what a rail with **nothing**
selected looks like. The one element whose whole job is to say "you are here"
said nothing, in the way that reads as normal.

Both rails now scroll the marked row into view when what is being browsed
changes. `block: 'nearest'` is the whole design: minimum distance, and nothing
at all when the row is already visible, so it can never yank a rail somebody has
scrolled themselves. Keyed on the app count as well, because `browsing` is
restored during mount and can land before there are any rows to find.

| state                     | scrollTop | marked row | visible |
| ------------------------- | --------- | ---------- | ------- |
| before, pinned on My Team | 0         | 925 -> 969 | **no**  |
| after, pinned on My Team  | 517       | 408 -> 452 | yes     |
| after, pinned on My Site  | **0**     | near top   | yes     |

The third row matters as much as the second. sparx restores a pinned module the
same way and has more modules than Piggles has apps, so it clips sooner; fixed
identically.

It had not been found because every previous look at this console was at a
window tall enough to show the whole rail. At 1113px nothing clips and
`scrollTop 0` is correct. It only exists at the height people actually work at,
and it presents as an absence.

| issue                                                            | severity | what                                                      | status |
